base: main f4a01ba6 (WP87 warm API; WP88 merged; WP90 trap guard not yet the default)
question: Does the frozen warm continuation (step and diagonal metric fixed at the tick-0 fit) degrade the 2 %/5 % sigma_next quote over 2,000 ticks and across a regime change on a fixed-lag SV window, and does a cheap periodic or drift-triggered re-adaptation fix it?

model.source: WP84/WP88 price-only SV target, density code copied verbatim (STUDIES/online_sv_quote_v2/rust/src/main.rs)

streams.shift: models/data-shift.json (regime 2 from return index 1250, i.e. entering at tick 1001)

stream.window: tick t conditions on returns [t, t + N) (fixed lag; the oldest return leaves, one enters)
stream.why_fixed_lag: the growing model (dimension 2,253 at tick 2,000) would cost about 1 s per warm tick and 4 min per reference tick, 3-4 h on two lanes; the fixed window keeps the regime change fully visible (window entirely regime 2 from tick 1,250) at 80 ms per tick
stream.remap: shift_window (harness): z'_0 = rho z_0 + sqrt(1 - rho^2) z_1, z'_i = z_{i+1} (i >= 1), z'_{N-1} = 0 (mass 1); masses: first latent keeps mass[3], the rest shift, new one 1; step unchanged; preserves h_1..h_{N-1} exactly (checked by `wp96 remapcheck` before the freeze)

arms.tick0: 4 x 1,000/1,000 at defaults, best-of-16 starts, chain gate (WarmupStep/SampledLogDensity chains dropped; < 2 left = cell failed)
arms.warm: Sampler::run_warm with draws(K) each tick; seed = seed*1_000_003 + 16*tick (chain c on +c)

policies.m100: re-adapt at every tick t with t % 100 == 0
policies.m500: re-adapt at every tick t with t % 500 == 0
policies.trig: re-adapt when the cost trigger fires (see trigger)

readapt.what: Sampler::run, warmup 200, draws 1, chains = carried chains, from the current positions, Metric::Diagonal{adapt: true, initial: elementwise geometric mean of the carried per-chain mass diagonals}, Adaptation default (dual averaging 0.8), seed tick_seed + 8; warm_state() replaces the carried state; a chain flagged WarmupStep/SampledLogDensity keeps its pre-re-adaptation state (per-chain fallback, counted); on a run error the state is unchanged (counted)
readapt.timed: the re-adaptation and the K-draw refresh of that tick are both inside the tick's wall

trigger.statistic: C_t = mean target evaluations per transition over the tick's chains x K transitions (run_warm's TransitionDiagnostics::target_evaluations); U_t = fraction of transitions with position_changed() == false
trigger.why_not_acceptance: run_warm runs retained transitions without acceptance capture, so TransitionDiagnostics::acceptance_statistic() is None there; the cost per transition is the quantity a frozen step/metric mismatch raises in both directions (refinement when too coarse, longer trajectories when too fine) and is what sets the latency
trigger.baseline: mean C over ticks a+1..a+20, a = latest adaptation tick (0 = the tick-0 fit)
trigger.trailing: mean C (and U) over ticks t-20..t-1
trigger.armed: at tick t once t - 1 >= a + 40 (so re-adaptations are at least 41 ticks apart)
trigger.fires: trailing C > 1.5 x baseline C, or trailing U > 0.05; evaluated at the start of tick t, a firing re-adapts at tick t

reference.arm: oWALNUTS defaults 4 x 2,000/20,000 on the tick's window, best-of-16 starts, Limits::admit_worst_case + max_result_bytes_unchecked(2 GiB)
reference.gate: drop chains named by a WarmupStep or SampledLogDensity chain warning; pass iff >= min_chains remain AND rank R-hat(h_next) over the remaining chains <= max_rhat (arviz)
reference.seed_rule: attempt a at tick t: seed_base*10000 + t + 5000*a; attempt 1 only when attempt 0 fails the gate (part of the cell definition, not a rerun)
reference.gate_failed: a tick failing both attempts is unscored and counts as a FAILED tick for every arm scored there
reference.one_per_stream: the reference depends on the data only, so it runs once per stream (not per arm seed): the same 162 fits the task's 41 x 2 x 2 would cost, spent on twice the scored ticks per half

quantities.h_next: mu + rho (h_last - mu) + exp(log_sigma) eps, eps[c,j] = default_rng(eps_seed_base+tick).normal(size=(4,20000))[c,j] (chain index c of the arm or reference)
reported: fraction of draws inside the reference 90 % interval
coverage of the true h_next by the arm's 90 % interval

accuracy.stuck_chain: median log_sigma more than 1.0 from the gated reference's median, or median h_last more than 2.0 away (WP84 census rule)
accuracy.tick_pass: |P50 err| <= 2 % AND |P95 err| <= 5 % AND no stuck chain (no latency condition in the pass; latency is reported)
accuracy.half_pass: per (arm, stream, half): pooled over the two seeds >= 95 % of scored ticks pass (>= 76/80) AND every seed >= 90 % (>= 36/40)
accuracy.arm_pass: an arm passes a stream iff it passes both halves

drift.statistic: per (arm, stream, seed, half): mean signed P50 error over the half's last 10 scored ticks minus its first 10
drift.role: reported with the bound flag, not part of the pass (10-tick windows have an sd of about 0.3 pp at K = 200)

latency.definition: wall per tick from new-target construction (including shift_window and any re-adaptation) to run_warm returned and warm_state() taken; writing draws excluded

decision.rule: the README may say 'the frozen warm path holds for 2,000 ticks and across a regime change' only if the frozen arm passes both halves on both streams (every seed >= 90 %, pooled >= 95 %); otherwise it names the re-adaptation policy (or policies) that passes both halves on both streams, with its latency median and P99

seeds.verified: 960101, 960102, 969450, 969500 grep-unused on main; 96096 (given) occurs only as a float substring

budget.wall_expected: about 1 h on two lanes after the build; 2 h cap
budget.breakdown: reference 81 ticks x ~12 s x 2 streams = 32 min; 16 warm cells x ~3-4 min = 60 min

execution.box: c7a.4xlarge owalnuts-bench, lanes 3 (cores 8-11, shift stream) and 4 (cores 12-15, control), taskset-pinned, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, co-tenanted (WP93 on cores 0-7): walls are 'pinned, co-tenanted'
execution.order: lane 3: ref-shift, then warm cells seed 960101 (frozen, m100, m500, trig), then seed 960102; lane 4 the same on control
execution.rule: cells sequential within a lane, each started once, never rerun; failures are results
